newsitem.title: NORWAY: N.Sea Sleipner East condensate output off 20-25pct.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Sleipner East condensate output off 20-25pct.

text.p: Condensate output at the North Sea Sleipner East development was running between 20 and 25 percent below normal due to gas compressor problems at the Kaarstoe terminal on Norway's west coast, operator Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Wednesday.
Statoil spokesman Trgyve Skanding said Sleipner East was producing around 400 tonnes per hour of condensate compared with a usual 500 tonnes per hour.
Gas exports to Kaarstoe were reduced by nearly 60 percent to around nine million cubic metres per day from 22 million cubic metres per day at full capacity, Skanding said.

Kaarstoe exports were hit following the unscheduled stoppage at one of three compressor units last week. A second compressor was already down for maintenance, leaving the plant operating at one third of capacity.

Skanding said Statoil expected to restart one compressor next Friday when condensate production was due to return to normal. The unit down for maintenance would return to operation on September 20, he said.
Oil exports from the Statfjord field have not been affected by the outage due to extra gas injection capacity at the development.
